At 36x earnings versus a seller-chosen peer median of 103x, the pricing leaves room for a pop, though much of that gap reflects the peer set being expensive in absolute terms rather than this issue being objectively cheap. Absent GMP and anchor data, this rests on subscription momentum and relative pricing alone.

longterm_view.reasoning: Growth and returns look exceptional (revenue CAGR ~54%, ROCE 70%), but profitability has not converted to cash: latest-year operating cash flow was only about 14% of EBITDA, and FY2024 operating cash flow was negative. Top-10 customers supply 93-95% of revenue [business, page 246], so the margin expansion story depends on a handful of buyers. High returns plus weak cash conversion plus extreme customer concentration is exactly the profile that can unwind quickly.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: The peer set is the seller's own selection and is skewed toward richly valued names (Hitachi Energy 159x, Schneider 155x, CG Power 115x); only Transformers & Rectifiers (32x) trades near the issue's 36x. So the apparent 0.35x discount to the median is largely a statement that the peer group itself is expensive, not proof that this issue is cheap; the most comparable-sounding peer by P/E prices it almost identically to Kanohar.

answers.question: check receivables and inventory against the sales growth
answers.answer: Revenue grew ~45% in the latest year while receivable days improved from 157.8 to 117.7, so receivables grew slower than sales — that part is not a red flag against the growth. But at 117 days collections are still very slow and cash conversion is only ~14% of EBITDA, so the working-capital burden of this growth is heavy; inventory data was not provided, so that leg cannot be checked.
